blocks.label: Shot 1
blocks.body: Medium shot, slow dolly in. He finishes taping, flexes the fist. Basement gym at 6am, condensation on the windows. practical lamps only. crushed blacks, high contrast grade. 3 seconds.

blocks.label: Shot 2
blocks.body: Medium shot, arc around subject. looks up at the camera. 3 seconds.

blocks.label: Shot 3
blocks.body: Medium shot, handheld follow. looks up at the camera. 3 seconds.

blocks.label: Audio
blocks.body: He says, "Last round." SFX: skipping rope on concrete. Ambient: distant traffic.

settings.name: Model
settings.why: O1 for unified generate-and-edit, Turbo for drafts

notes: Kling's own formula is shot type, movement direction, duration or speed descriptor, then style elements. Forge writes one block per shot in that order.
Master Shots camera presets are more stable than prompted camera language. When the move matters, use the preset.
Bind elements. Without them, identity drifts badly past about eight seconds.
warnings: Multi-shot auto-planning is on by default in some modes. If you want one continuous take you must say so explicitly.
Audio is billed per second and on by default. Turn it off for silent b-roll or you burn about a third extra.

variations.name: Colder, more documentary
variations.text: Swap the grade for desaturated earth tones, drop to available light only, and shoot it on a 35mm at f/2.8. Same subject, no styling.

variations.name: Tighter and more graphic
variations.text: Go to an extreme close-up on the single most telling detail. Hard directional light, deep shadow, generous negative space around it.

variations.name: Wider, with context
variations.text: Pull back to an establishing wide. Put the subject small in the frame and let the setting carry the story. Keep the same light and grade.
